name: Rosetta
first: First spacecraft to orbit a comet — and to land on one (Philae, 2014-11-12)
description: ESA's flagship comet-rendezvous mission. After a 10-year cruise that wove three Earth assists, a Mars assist, two asteroid flybys, and 957 days of deep-space hibernation, Rosetta caught up with comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko in August 2014 and orbited it for over two years through perihelion and out the back side. The Philae lander reached 67P's surface 2014-11-12 — the first soft landing on a comet — and returned ~64 hours of science after a harpoon failure left it in the shadow of a cliff. Rosetta itself ended the mission with a controlled descent to 67P's surface on 2016-09-30. Key results: organic molecules and glycine in the coma; 67P's initially-measured D/H ratio (≈3× terrestrial) argued against Jupiter-family comets as Earth's water source — a result a 2024 re-analysis has since called into question after finding a measurement error; the first detailed maps of comet outgassing geometry.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Ariane 5G+ lifts Rosetta from Kourou for the 10-year cruise to comet 67P.

events.label: EARTH FLYBY #1
events.note: First of three Earth gravity assists to build velocity for the comet rendezvous.

events.label: MARS FLYBY
events.note: Single Mars gravity assist + first close imagery of Phobos and Mars at 250 km.

events.label: ASTEROID 2867 ŠTEINS
events.note: First-ever close-up of an E-type asteroid.

events.label: ASTEROID 21 LUTETIA
events.note: ~120 km flyby of one of the largest main-belt asteroids ever observed close-up.

events.label: COMET 67P RENDEZVOUS
events.note: Orbit insertion around comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko. Philae lands 2014-11-12.
